title: Pitch link to pitch plate grip length
description: Built from scratch against the drawings and the NAS standards. Three of its eight elements carry an unverified band -- two applied 2026-09-15 by operator ruling, and the eye a loudly-marked catalog placeholder whose bearing identity awaits the 213862-002 drawing.

joint.description: The 5-place joint in DETAIL B: NAS6403U11D bolt down through the pitch-link eye (spherical bearing) and a plain bushing, through a 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, retained by a slotted nut + cotter pin over a flat washer. DETAIL B shows TWO grip stacks of identical architecture: this one (5 places, -11 bolt) and the tangential-link joint analysed in slice 1 (3 places, -14 bolt).

parts.role: bolt, .190-32 x .688 grip, unplated, drilled shank
plain bushing, .1900 in ID x .1875 in long (8 = 3 tangential-link places + 5 here)
PITCH PLATE ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW -- contains the 215735 pitch plate

joint.clamped: The bolt clamps, in order from its head: the 214820-002 bushing, the pitch-link eye (modelled since 2026-09-15 as the MS14101-3 ball width, a loudly-marked placeholder -- see that element), the NAS77A3-015A flanged bushing's flange (press-fit in the plate assembly, added 2026-09-15), the 4.06 mm pitch-plate lug, and the NAS1149V0332H washer. Retention is the MS9363-09 slotted nut with an MS24665-153 cotter pin through the drilled shank ('D' suffix, NAS6403 sheet 2 CODE block).
joint.question: Does the NAS6403U11D (.688 in grip) work in this joint -- i.e. does the end of its full cylindrical shank clear the nut bearing face (JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5), and does its cotter hole sit clear of the clamped stack?
joint.scope: Grip length only, and only along the bolt axis. Out of scope, deliberately: diameter and hole fits (simple two-component fits); bushing-to-bore interference (JPS00176); the pitch link's own internal stack; the joint at the other end of the pitch link; torque and preload.
joint.identification_note: No part in the 217755 parts list is named 'pitch link'. This joint is identified as Jeff's 'pitch link to pitch plate' by elimination and corroboration, not by nomenclature: (1) his note says the joint is visible in the same view as the tangential-link joint, and DETAIL B contains exactly two grip stacks; (2) slice 1 claimed the 3X / -14 stack as the tangential link, matching 212956-005 PITCH ANTI ROTATION LINK ASSEMBLY at qty 3; (3) this one is 5 places, the propeller has FIVE blades (217755 sheet 2 FRONT VIEW), and one pitch link per blade gives five; (4) the pitch plate part drawing 215197 carries a distinct 5X 4.06 +/-0.10 flange group, separate from the 3X +/-0.08 (tangential) and 1X +/-0.10 (VPA) groups. [2026-09-16, handoff citation_identity_correctness: that reading stands and is recorded as made -- it was made on 215197 A.1, the PRELIM fixture. The released plate is a different part number, 215735 rev A, and its sheet 2 prints the same three groups at the same addresses, so the elimination argument carries over unchanged. The 215735-A sheet 1 now prints TWO 4.06 +/-0.10 callouts rather than one, which widens the VPA group but does not touch the 5X/3X distinction this argument turns on.] The link part number -- gap 1 from founding until 2026-09-15 -- is 213862-002 PITCH LINK ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER: item 24, qty 5, of the 216231 A.1 HUB AND BLADE ASSEMBLY parts list (`data/inbox/specs/[2025-OCT-9 FOR SNS101-M1 BUILD] 216231 A.1.pdf`), the qty matching this joint's five places where 212956-005's three cannot. Its own drawing, which would name its bearing, is not in any repo this session can read -- the eye element's placeholder marker and the operator queue both point at it.

grip end to point, i.e. the standard's T (Ref) -- a provenance cross-check, not a design quantity

checks.label: shank out, NAS6403U11D
checks.guidance: clamped column minus grip. Negative means the end of the full cylindrical shank sits proud of the nut bearing face, so the nut would engage incomplete threads -- which JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5 forbids outright ('The nut, nutplate, insert, part body, etc., shall not engage any incomplete threads of the bolt shank'). COMPLETE SINCE 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit): the pitch-link eye and the NAS77A3-015A flange, this column's two missing members, are now terms, so the verdict speaks for the modelled joint -- but THREE of the five column terms are unverified (the eye a loudly-marked placeholder whose bearing identity needs the 213862-002 drawing, the bushing an operator reading, the washer a workbook band), so read the verdict with `worst_confidence: untraced` in view. It PASSES worst case by 0.1098 mm (column at min 17.8390 against grip at max 17.7292) -- a thin margin that a wrong placeholder erases: if the eye were the WIDE MS14103-3 (11.05/11.10) the check would read +4.0 mm and the cotter-hole check would go negative, which is one of the reasons the narrow bearing is the credible candidate. Until 2026-09-15 this check was a BUDGET (the eye was excluded for want of any source) and its magnitude read as the eye width the joint requires: >= 8.4280 mm worst case -- a requirement the MS14101-3 ball width (7.09/7.14) does NOT meet on its own; the flange member found the missing 1.45-1.57 mm, which is exactly why a member-completeness sweep and not a value fix was what this joint needed.

checks.label: cotter hole clear of the clamped column

configuration.nut: MS9363-09 slotted -- height and castellation geometry unsourced

excluded_terms: MS9363-09 nut height and thread-start-to-castellation distance -- the height is printed in MS9363 Rev C (spec-library subject MS9363-09, H = .178/.198 in) but deliberately not folded, because the quantity that decides cotter installability is the castellation PHASE, which no document controls (JPS00094 5.9.7's washer-swap procedure is the remedy); folding the height alone would dress an unanswerable alignment question as a linear one
checks.guidance: Head-to-cotter-hole minus the clamped column. Since 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit) the column is all five members -- the eye rides in as the loudly-marked MS14101-3 placeholder -- so what is left over must cover only the nut side: the MS9363-09's height up to a castellation slot, which stays excluded (see excluded_terms) because the slot-to-thread-start phase is uncontrolled by any document. It passes with 2.3296 mm worst case available (nominal 3.1662, max 4.3098); an MS9363-09 at its max height (5.0292 mm) does NOT fit inside the worst-case budget, which is the castellation/washer-selection story again, not a new finding. Before the eye and flange were terms this budget read 11.0444 mm worst case and had to cover the eye too. It cannot settle the joint either way: with a slotted nut and a cotter pin the constraint is slot-vs-hole ALIGNMENT, which quantises acceptable grip -- see the notes and the worksheet. Note the wide-bearing counterfactual: with MS14103-3 in the eye this budget's worst case would be NEGATIVE (-1.63 mm), i.e. the cotter hole inside the clamped stack -- independent corroboration that the narrow bearing is the credible candidate.

Every element is an additive external length or a hole location; there is no chamfer, relief or counterbore, so `max == mmc` on all seven elements that carry lmc/mmc, and `cotter_hole_from_point` carries neither, because it is a location and 'most material' has no meaning for where a hole sits. The only negative signs in this file are on whole-element/whole-path subtractions.

QUANTISED GRIP -- THE MODEL DOES NOT SETTLE THIS JOINT. Retention is MS9363-09 (NUT, SLOTTED, HEXAGON, SHEAR) plus MS24665-153 cotter pin through the drilled shank. The governing constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the bolt's cotter hole, which quantises acceptable grip into discrete workable values instead of bounding it in a continuous interval. JPS00094 Rev C section 5.9.7 states the remedy in as many words -- 'If the hole and nut castellation do not align, change/add a washer or a different nut, and try again' with a footnote that 'Different nuts likely have different manufactured thread-start to castellation-hole spacing' -- and section 5.5.3.a caps the remedy at three washers per fastener. So this is assembly-time selection by specification, and no grip interval computed here can replace it. The two documents that would close it: MS9363 (slot count and depth) and the nut height; the bolt side is already closed by NAS6403 sheet 1 M = .174/.154.

Element order is the physical order from the bolt head: bushing, pitch-link eye, flanged-bushing flange, pitch-plate lug, washer; the three fastener dimensions follow. Only the path term lists are load-bearing for the arithmetic.
